help.twitch.title: Set up Twitch monitoring
help.twitch.intro: For Twitch mode, the managed API only needs the channel login. Own Twitch credentials are optional.
help.twitch.step1: Enter only the Twitch channel name in Streamer Login, not the full Twitch URL.
help.twitch.step2: Leave Managed API selected for the easiest setup.
help.twitch.step3: Optional: switch to Own Twitch app if you want to use direct Twitch API credentials.
help.twitch.step4: For Own Twitch app, open the Twitch Developer Console and create a new application.
help.twitch.step5: Copy the Client ID and create a Client Secret with New Secret. Keep the secret private and never share it.
help.twitch.note: Managed API is the easiest mode. Switch to Own Twitch app only if you want to use your own Client ID and Client Secret.
help.discord.title: Set up a Discord app
help.discord.intro: For this app, the important Discord value is the Application ID, also called the Client ID. A bot token is not required.
help.discord.step1: Open the Discord Developer Portal and create a new application.
help.discord.step2: Give the application a name and optionally add an icon or description so it looks cleaner in Discord.
help.discord.step3: Open General Information and copy the Application ID. Discord also refers to it as the Client ID.
help.discord.step4: Paste that ID into the Discord block in this app.
help.discord.step5: If you want image keys to work, upload the art assets in your Discord application first and then enter those keys in this app.
help.discord.note: You do not need to create a bot token just to use Rich Presence with this app.
help.usage.title: How to use the app
help.usage.intro: Choose the mode first, then fill only the matching blocks plus the Discord Application ID.
help.usage.step1: Pick Twitch, YouTube, or Custom Rich Presence in the source area at the top of the dashboard.
help.usage.step2: Twitch and YouTube monitor live status automatically. Discord Rich Presence lets you set activity type, details, state, timestamps, images, and buttons yourself.
help.usage.step3: Enter the Discord Application ID in the Discord block.
help.usage.step4: Twitch and YouTube use the Images block. Discord Rich Presence has its own image fields directly inside the custom block.
help.usage.step5: Use Test Connection first. After that, save your settings or create a preset if you need multiple setups.
help.usage.step6: Start Presence from the dashboard or enable auto-start in Settings. The preview and stream info area help you verify the result first.
help.usage.note: Discord desktop must already be running, otherwise Rich Presence cannot be set.
help.support.title: Where to get help
help.support.intro: For Twitch, YouTube, or Discord platform questions, use the official developer pages below. For this app itself, use the place where you got the project if a support page exists there.
help.support.step1: Use Twitch documentation and the Twitch developer forum for Twitch app setup, authentication, and API questions.
help.support.step2: Use the YouTube Data API documentation or Google Cloud help for API keys, quota, and channel lookup questions.
help.support.step3: Use the Discord Developer Help Center for Application ID, Developer Portal, and Discord app setup questions.
help.support.step4: Use the general Discord Help Center if the issue is with the Discord desktop client instead of developer setup.
help.support.note: Helpful bug reports include the app version, your Windows version, screenshots, the exact error message, and short reproduction steps.
help.tips.title: Useful tips
help.tips.intro: A few small details help avoid the most common setup mistakes.
help.tips.step1: Never share your Twitch Client Secret, YouTube API key, or other private project credentials with anyone.
help.tips.step2: The check interval must still be at least 5 seconds. YouTube offline checks are additionally throttled internally.
help.tips.step3: Stream images remain optional for Twitch and YouTube, and Discord Rich Presence images remain optional inside the custom block.
help.tips.step4: Use presets if you switch between Twitch channels, YouTube channels, Discord apps, or different custom Rich Presence setups.
help.tips.step5: Export your settings before larger changes so you always have a backup.
help.tips.step6: If the interface looks stuck or wrong after changes, use Reload in the title bar or restart the app once.
hint.youtubeQuota: Offline YouTube checks are throttled to protect your API quota.

help.twitch.step6: Choose Twitch Stream as the source if Discord Presence should automatically follow Twitch live status.
help.youtube.title: Set up YouTube support
help.youtube.intro: For YouTube mode, you need a Google API key with access to the YouTube Data API v3 and a channel ID, handle, or channel URL.
help.youtube.step1: Open Google Cloud Console and create a project or choose an existing one.
help.youtube.step2: Enable the YouTube Data API v3 for that project.
help.youtube.step3: Create an API key under Credentials and keep it private.
help.youtube.step4: Paste the API key into the YouTube block in this app.
help.youtube.step5: Paste a channel ID, an @handle, or a full YouTube channel URL into the channel field.
help.youtube.step6: Choose YouTube Stream as the source if Discord Presence should automatically follow live videos from that channel.
help.youtube.note: Offline checks are throttled in the background so your YouTube API quota is not consumed too quickly.
help.usage.step7: Presets also store the selected mode and all advanced custom Rich Presence fields.
help.support.step5: If you want to report a bug or request a feature for this app, use the project page, GitHub issues, Discord server, or release post where the app was shared.
